mamba-130m-hf · 24 Mamba blocks, width 768, inner width 1536, SSM state 16, conv kernel 4 · 2 checkpoints: init, trained
A cell is (checkpoint, layer, position, view) after t tokens read. Dots: the 36 residual cells per checkpoint. Right: each block's recurrent state, conv buffer c and SSM state z; the column is the whole state Σt, everything the model carries forward.

I gave a small selective state-space model, mamba-130m-hf, the same 1,000 text snippets as the Pythia study (200 each of maths, code, Wikipedia, forum posts and poetry), recorded its residual stream and its recurrent state at six layers, after six numbers of tokens read, at two checkpoints (the HF initialisation and the trained model), and asked which snippets it treats alike, with the label-free construction used on the ResNet and on Pythia. The reason to look at Mamba: after reading $t$ tokens it holds a fixed-size state, and that state is everything it carries forward, so the whole of it can be measured directly, one vector per snippet per position.

The idea in one example. Fix layer 16 of the trained model. After 16 tokens, centre the residual vectors over the snippets and compare every pair by cosine, link each snippet to its 15 nearest, and turn the links into a random walk between snippets. Do the same after 4, 8, 32, 64 and 128 tokens: six walks over the same snippets, in six different geometries. Their average is the walk of a reading block (a run of cells along the reading axis; not a Mamba block). Its slowest-changing functions, made sparse, give a few coherent sets. Then ask the same of layer 16's own recurrent state, and of the states of all layers up to 16; at layer 24 the latter is the model's whole state. Sources are never used, only checked afterwards.

The targets were written before the run (SPEC section 7) and are scored below by the build, from the data. Of the 7 hypotheses: met, 5 (H3, H4, H5, H6, H7); not met, 2 (H1, H2); not decidable from this data, 0 (none). Of the 6 controls: pass, 4; fail, none; not run on this data, C1a, C1b.

The residual against the whole state, at the last layer and $t = 128$: span agreement $a_3$ = 0.33 (null 0.003), matched Jaccard of the sets 0.38. Source separation $\tilde W$ at $t = 128$: whole state 0.74, best residual layer 0.70. Mamba against Pythia on the same snippets, point against point at $t = 128$: $a_3$ 0.31 to 0.99 (from cross_arch.json).

How to read this mockup

Everything on this page is drawn from a synthetic fixture pushed through the real pipeline. Its items carry a planted three-level hierarchy (eight groups of 125) whose strength grows along layers; one layer (L8) carries a different, planted split instead. The state and stack views are fed by synthetic constituents (two per layer, with unequal item norms and non-zero means), so the state Gram identity and every page element run. Tokens and text are fake syllables, and the five "sources" are assigned in runs that follow the planted groups, so they line up with the structure only partly. The Mamba-against-Pythia comparison is between the two studies' fixtures, which plant the same seeded groups, so it agrees almost perfectly by construction. If the page works, the explorer shows four tight groups at the deeper layers in every view, the zoom recovers the planted groups for T1, and the initialisation looks structureless. The answer in words, and the Findings, will be written from the real data.

Open the explorer at this view

The question

In a causal transformer, what is carried forward from a prefix is the KV cache, which grows with $t$; the Pythia study could reach it only through a proxy, the prefix slab. A selective state-space model carries a fixed-size recurrent state instead. After reading token $t$, layer $l$ holds a convolution buffer and an SSM state, and the collection of these over all 24 layers is everything the model keeps about the prefix. I asked five things.

  1. Where does the walk separate kinds of text? Along reading and depth, at initialisation and trained: does maths part from poetry, and from how many tokens on?
  2. Token or source? How strongly is the walk tied to the token just read, and how strongly to the snippet's source?
  3. Residual, layer state or whole state? Do the sets from the residual at position $t$ agree with those from layer $l$'s own recurrent state, and with those from the states of all layers up to $l$ (at $l$ = 24, the whole state)? Where along reading and depth do they part?
  4. What does zooming show? Cut a block's snippets in two with the block's own walk, redo the analysis on each half, and repeat; once on the whole state.
  5. Mamba against Pythia. On the same 1,000 snippets (both models read the Pile with the same tokenizer), how far do the two models' coherent sets agree at matched relative depth?

What is measured

For each cell $c$ (a checkpoint, a layer, a position and a view) the construction builds a random walk $P_c$ between the snippets from their cosine similarities (the procedure is below). A block $B$ is a run of cells along one axis, and everything on the page comes from the block's average walk.

$$ f^\top (I - \bar P_B)\, f \;=\; \frac{1}{|B|}\sum_{c \in B} f^\top (I - P_c)\, f \;=\; \frac{1}{|B|}\sum_{c \in B} \tfrac12 \sum_{i,j} (P_c)_{ij}\,(f_i - f_j)^2 $$
$$ S_c(\mathcal G) = \frac1N \sum_{g \in \mathcal G}\ \sum_{i \ne j \in g} (P_c)_{ij}, \qquad \tilde S = \frac{S - S^0}{1 - S^0} $$

where $f$ is any function on the $N$ snippets and $\bar P_B$ the mean of the cells' walks; a function that changes little across every walk step in every cell of the block has a small penalty (1), and the block's eigenfunctions $\psi_k$ are the functions with the smallest. $S_c(\mathcal G)$ is the share of the walk that stays inside the groups of a grouping $\mathcal G$, $S^0$ its chance level, and $\tilde S$ the excess over chance (0 for a walk that ignores the grouping, 1 for one that never leaves it). $\boldsymbol{T}$ groups snippets by the token at position $t$ (label-free: tokens are inputs); $\boldsymbol{W}$ groups them by source (validation).

$T$ and $W$ are associations between the walk and a grouping. They do not split the walk into a "token part" and a "context part", and nothing on this page reads them that way.

The recurrent state, and the three views

After the step that reads token $t$, layer $m$ holds a conv buffer $c^m_t$ (the last three inputs to its depthwise convolution, 4,608 numbers) and an SSM state $z^m_t$ (24,576 numbers). The tuple $\Sigma_t = (c^m_t, z^m_t)_{m=1}^{ 24 }$ (700,416 numbers), with the tokens after $t$, determines every later residual, state and next-token distribution [thm]: that is the recurrence itself, and control C1b checks it on the measured state. The residual $h^l_t$ is not a state: what layer $l+1$ does next depends on its own state, which is not a function of $h^l_t$ alone.

view$\phi(i)$ at (checkpoint, layer $l$, position $t$)
point$h^l_t(i)$, the residual stream after block $l$ (768 numbers)
statelayer $l$'s own state: the conv buffer and the SSM state, each through the standard step, cosine matrices averaged with equal weight
stackthe states of layers 1 to $l$: the same average over all $2l$ constituents. At $l$ = 24 this is the whole state $\Sigma_t$
bag (reference)the mean input embedding of tokens 1 to $t$: a function of the token counts alone

Labels

The method uses no labels. A snippet's source is used only to assemble a balanced probe, to colour plots, for the validation statistics ($W$, the pair mixing ratio $X$, matched Jaccard against sources), and to choose which snippets the "follow" figure shows. Source never enters a kernel, an operator, a basis, a cut or the choice of a block.

Cells and blocks

There are 72 cells per view: two checkpoints (the HF initialisation and the trained model) by six layers (L4, L8, L12, L16, L20, L24) by six positions (t = 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128); with three views and the bag, 228 in all. A block runs along exactly one axis: a reading block is one layer at positions 4 to 128 (trained, in any view), and a depth block is one position at layers L4 to L24 (trained, point view). A single cell is also a block. No intermediate training checkpoints of mamba-130m are published, so there is no training axis; the initialisation is a comparison, like Pythia's step 0. Positions are roughly log-spaced, so with equal weights per cell, early reading counts for more per token than late reading.

The procedure in five steps

Five fixed computations, from activations to sets, unchanged from the ResNet and Pythia studies. The pictures use the cell (L16, t = 128) and the point reading block of L16 at the trained checkpoint; in every matrix the snippets are in the order of that block's first zoom cut. Exact statements are in Method.

1. Compare snippets within one cell

Take every snippet's vector in one cell, centre it over the 1,000 snippets, scale each vector to unit length, and take the cosine between every pair. That cosine is the only geometry the construction assumes. For the state and stack views the same is done for each constituent (each conv buffer and each SSM state) separately, and the cosine matrices are averaged, so that no constituent's scale decides the weighting.

2. Turn similarity into a walk

Link two snippets if either is among the other's 15 nearest neighbours (weight 1, a floor of $10^{-6}$ elsewhere). Symmetric Sinkhorn scaling turns these links into a walk $P_c$ whose rows and columns sum to 1, so every snippet carries the same weight. The lazy walk $M_c = \tfrac12(I + P_c)$ stays put half the time.

3. Average over a block

A block's operator $\bar M$ is the plain average of its cells' lazy walks. No map between cells is fitted: each cell keeps its own geometry, and the cells meet only through the snippets they share.

4. Take its eigenfunctions, with their retention in every cell

The leading eigenvectors $\psi_1, \psi_2, \ldots$ of $\bar M$ are the functions on the snippets with the smallest average penalty (1). An average can hide a cell where the function varies a lot, so next to each eigenfunction I show its retention $\rho_c(\psi_k) = \psi_k^\top M_c \psi_k$ in each cell: 1 means the function is constant on every walk neighbourhood of that cell, and a random function with mean zero gets about 0.5.

5. Sparse vectors, coherent sets

SEBA rotates the first $r$ eigenvectors (with the constant $\psi_0$) into $r$ sparse, non-negative vectors. Each snippet goes to the vector on which it is largest, or is unassigned if all are zero. The page shows $r = 2$ and $r = 4$. These coherent sets are the groups on which the averaged walk's slowest functions concentrate.

The explorer is meant for a laptop or desktop screen: panels are small here, and hovering a point (to read its snippet) needs a mouse.

How to use the explorer

The grid. Rows are layers and a bag reference row; columns are positions t, the number of snippet tokens read. The View switch chooses what a layer row measures: the point view (the residual stream after block l at t), the state view (layer l's own recurrent state after t tokens) or the stack view (the states of layers 1 to l; at L24 that is everything the model carries forward). Every panel shows the same 1,000 snippets at one cell, placed by a 2-d layout of that cell in that view. The layouts are for display only; no number on this page is computed from them. Under the grid, a strip shows one layer at t = 128 at the HF initialisation and trained.

Pick a block. Click a panel for that cell alone, a row label for the layer's reading block (t = 4 to 128, in the current view), a column header for the position's depth block (L4 to L24, point view), or a strip panel for that cell at either checkpoint. The block's averaged walk gives the colours, which are painted on every panel so you can follow the same snippets elsewhere.

Read the side panel. Sets with their snippets and source make-up (validation only), the spectrum, the walk shares $\tilde T$ and $\tilde W$, and the retention of each function in every cell along the block's axis. Hover a point to read its snippet up to that panel's position.

  1. Pick a view and a block. point, state or stack; then a panel, a row label or a column header.
  2. Hover a point. The same snippet is ringed in every panel.
  3. Read the side panel. Sets, snippets, spectrum, retention.

Zoom

Take a block, cut its snippets in two with the block's own averaged walk, redo the whole analysis on each half, and repeat. Each half is treated as a new probe: its cells are rebuilt on those snippets alone. The tree shows where the walk keeps finding a cheap cut and where it stops.

How a node is cut. A cut divides the node's snippets into two sides. For the node's snippets alone, I rebuild each cell of the block (centred over those snippets, 15 nearest neighbours among them), average the walks, and try every threshold on each of the averaged walk's three slowest functions $\psi_1, \psi_2, \psi_3$. The cut kept is the one with the lowest conductance $\phi^*$: the share of walk steps that cross it, relative to the smaller side. Both sides need at least $\max(16, 5\%\ \text{of}\ n)$ snippets. SEBA with $r = 2$, run on the same walk, is shown beside the cut but never makes it. Nodes are split to depth 3, or until fewer than 64 snippets remain.

How a split is read. Compare the cut's cost with how fast the walk mixes otherwise. $\mu_2$ is the walk's second-slowest rate of mixing; the clustering ratio $\Upsilon = \mu_2 / \phi^*$ is large when the cut is much cheaper than anything else the walk offers, as for two groups with few links between them. I draw splits with $\Upsilon \ge 3$ as clear and the rest as weak (lighter, dashed outline; still clickable). The threshold was fixed before any real tree was opened, on synthetic data where the answer is known: planted groups gave $\Upsilon \ge$ 8.26, pure noise 1.4 to 1.88. Those are reference points, not a test: the noise was isotropic and 32-dimensional, and $\Upsilon$ for structureless data depends on the geometry. $\Upsilon$ changes only how a split is drawn, never whether the recursion continues.

loading…

Observed. T1's first cut puts 100 % of maths, 100 % of code, 50 % of wiki, 0 % of forum, 0 % of poetry on one side (child 0) (H6: met). Its clustering ratio is 688; the 28 splits of the four trees have $\Upsilon$ between 1.97 to 1.11e+05 (T1 8.42 to 688, T2 1.97 to 4.02, T3 5.19 to 451, T4 on the whole state 1.99 to 1.11e+05); at or above the threshold: 19 of 28. The largest number of connected pieces in any split node's kNN graph is 8. SEBA with $r = 2$ agrees with the cut at matched Jaccard 0.12 to 1.00 across nodes. The root cut's retention in the six cells of T1's block is 1.00.

The threshold was calibrated on isotropic synthetic noise in 32 dimensions, not on anything resembling a residual stream or a recurrent state; it is a reference point, not a test.

The four trees
  • T1 (the headline): the point reading block of L16, t = 4 to 128, trained.
  • T2: the point reading block of L4, trained, an early-layer contrast.
  • T3: the single cell (L16, t = 128), point view, to compare one cell with a block.
  • T4: the whole-state reading block (stack view at L24, t = 4 to 128), trained: the zoom on everything the model keeps. On each subset it repeats the stack view's own construction: each of the 48 constituents' raw inner-product matrices is restricted to the subset, re-centred and normalised there, and only then averaged.

All four are precomputed; no recursion runs in the browser. Why the subset is rebuilt rather than restricted: restricting each cell's kernel (or, for T4, the parent's averaged Gram) to $S$ leaves snippets near the cut with few neighbours, whose floor links Sinkhorn then inflates, and keeps the parent's split direction as a common offset. A probe made of $S$ is centred over $S$, so the rebuild is what "the same analysis on those snippets" means.

Measurements

The measurements behind the verdict, one question at a time. Captions say what is plotted; the paragraph after each figure gives the numbers it rests on, all computed from the data. Every figure draws from the embedded data: hover for values.

Q0. Do the controls hold?

Three identities and three planted checks come first. C1a checks that recurrent decoding, which is how the state is read, gives the same residuals as the model's parallel forward pass. C1b checks that the measured state is the state: a fresh decode started at $t = 64$ from nothing but the stored conv buffers and SSM states continues exactly as the original. C2 checks that the bag view depends only on token counts. P1 runs the zoom on a synthetic hierarchy with a known answer and fixes the reading threshold for $\Upsilon$ before any real tree is looked at.

Observed. C1a: not run: fixture has no model (not run). C1b: not run: fixture has no model (not run). C2: init: max |difference| 0; trained: max |difference| 0 (pass). P1: exact; planted Υ ≥ 8.26, structureless ≤ 1.88; threshold 3 (pass). P2: sweep / SEBA Jaccard: transient cell 1.00 / 1.00, block 1.00 / 1.00 (pass). P3: block means: largest deviation 1.9e-15; Gram identity (state, stack at t = 128): 1.1e-15 (tolerance 1e-12) (pass). The T4 raw-Gram route matches the stored whole-state Grams to 1.27e-14. C1a's float32 discrepancy, a reported hazard rather than a gate, is n/a (not run on this data).

Which blocks find sets that line up with sources?

The questions below are about walk shares and agreement. This one is about the coherent sets themselves: compare each block's $r = 4$ sets with the five sources (validation only).

Observed. As a share of the best score their set sizes allow, the reading blocks reach 0.17 to 0.81 (point), 0.81 (state) and 0.78 to 0.81 (stack), against a null of at most 0.16; point single cells reach 0.17 to 0.81 of theirs, and 30 of 36 of them beat their own null. At $t = 128$ the state cells give 0.58 to 0.65 and the stack cells 0.42 to 0.65 (whole state: 0.42); the bag cell gives 0.86.

Q1. Is the walk tied to the token just read, or to the source?

In plain words: $\tilde T$ is how much more often than chance a walk step joins two snippets that read the same token at position $t$; $\tilde W$ is the same for two snippets from the same source. Both are 0 for a walk that ignores the grouping and 1 for one that never leaves it. The two checkpoints sit side by side on one colour scale.

Observed. Trained: $\tilde T$ is -0.00 to 0.00 at L4 across positions and 0.00 at L24 (H1: not met; T̃ at L4 minus L24: -0.001, -0.000, -0.000, -0.001, -0.002, -0.003). At initialisation $\tilde T$ at L4 is -0.00 to 0.00, and $\tilde W$ is 0.01 to 0.10 across the point cells. Trained, at L16, $\tilde W$ is 0.70 at $t = 4$, 0.69 at 32 and 0.69 at 128; from $t = 4$ to 128 it changes by -0.00, -0.01, -0.01, 0.00 at L12 to L24 (H2: not met); it peaks at $t$ = 16, 4, 32, 128 in those layers. The largest point value anywhere is 0.70; the bag row goes from 0.13 at $t = 4$ to 0.85 at 128.

Q2. When does the walk stop linking maths and poetry?

The pair mixing ratio $X(A, B)$ is the walk mass between sources $A$ and $B$, scaled so that a walk ignoring sources gives 1. Below 1, the walk avoids crossing between them. Wikipedia against forum posts is the prose-to-prose contrast.

To see what this means for single snippets, follow two of them. The ten follow items are the first two of each source in probe order, which is random, so the choice does not depend on any result.

Observed. Trained, point view: $X(\text{maths}, \text{poetry})$ at (L16, 16) is 0.00 against a permutation band of 0.94 to 1.07 (H3: met); at initialisation the same cell gives 0.79. Ranked from most to least separated among the pairs at (L16, 16), maths and poetry are number 4 of 10; code against poetry is 0.00, wiki against forum 0.71. The first $t$ at which it falls below 0.5 is 4, 4, 4, 4 at L12, L16, L20 and L24; it is 0.00 to 0.01 for $t \ge 32$ there, 0.23 to 0.31 at L4, and 0.247 for the bag at $t = 128$. The default follow snippets (items 9 and 4) send 0.93 to 1.00 and 0.81 to 1.00 of their L16 walk to their own source across positions, and share a single-cell $r = 4$ set in 0 of 36 trained cells.

Q3. Residual, layer state or whole state?

Three views of the same (layer, position) are compared. The point view is the residual after block $l$ at $t$. The state view is layer $l$'s own recurrent state after $t$ tokens. The stack view is the states of layers 1 to $l$; at L24 it is the whole state, everything the model carries forward. Agreement between the views' eigenfunctions asks whether they organise the snippets the same way; it is not a measure of information. The state and stack views weight each constituent equally after its own normalisation (decision D-M1).

Observed. Across layers and positions, $a_3$ is 0.00 to 1.00 for point vs layer state, 0.00 to 1.00 for point vs stack and 0.30 to 1.00 for layer state vs stack (0.00 to 1.00, 0.00 to 0.97 and 0.34 to 0.99 at $t = 128$). The residual against the whole state at L24 gives 0.33 to 0.49 over positions. The sets' matched Jaccard is 0.15 to 1.00, 0.15 to 1.00 and 0.31 to 1.00 (nulls at most 0.17, 0.17, 0.17). At $t = 128$, $\tilde W$ is -0.00 to 0.70 for the point view across layers, 0.42 to 0.73 for the layer state and 0.57 to 0.74 for the stack; the whole state gives 0.74 against 0.70 for the L24 residual (H4: met). Diagnostic for D-M1: each constituent alone against the state view gives $a_3$ 0.73 to 0.97 (conv buffer) and 0.77 to 1.00 (SSM state).

Q4. What does training add to the initialisation?

The initialisation is MambaForCausalLM(config) after torch.manual_seed(0), i.e. Hugging Face's re-implementation of the Mamba reference init, not the authors' saved initial state. It plays the role of Pythia's step 0.

Observed. $\tilde W$ at (L16, 128), point view, is 0.08 at initialisation and 0.69 trained (H5: met). Over all cells at initialisation, $\tilde W$ is 0.01 to 0.10 (point), 0.01 to 0.13 (state) and 0.03 to 0.37 (stack). The initialisation's sets against the trained sets, matched Jaccard at (L16, 16) and (L16, 128): point 0.25 (a₃ 0.14; null up to 0.16) and 0.21 (a₃ 0.13; null up to 0.16); state 0.21 (a₃ 0.11; null up to 0.16) and 0.23 (a₃ 0.15; null up to 0.16); stack 0.44 (a₃ 0.38; null up to 0.17) and 0.34 (a₃ 0.29; null up to 0.15).

Q5. Does the order of the earlier tokens matter?

For each snippet, the reordered probe S shuffles tokens 1 to 127 and keeps token 128, and is read at $t = 128$ only. The two probes then have the same snippets, the same token counts and the same last token, so comparing them changes only the order of the earlier tokens. The bag view cannot tell them apart (C2). This is an association, not a causal claim about what the model uses.

Observed. Matched Jaccard between the original and reordered probes' sets: point L4 0.55, L8 0.33, L12 0.97, L16 1.00, L20 0.99, L24 1.00; state L4 0.77, L8 0.97, L12 0.99, L16 1.00, L20 1.00, L24 1.00; stack L4 0.99, L8 1.00, L12 1.00, L16 0.50, L20 0.50, L24 0.50 (null means 0.08 to 0.16).

Q6. Mamba against Pythia on the same snippets

Both models were trained on the Pile with the same tokenizer, and the Pythia probe is reused verbatim, so item $i$ is the same snippet in both studies and their cells can be compared directly: span agreement between the two models' eigenfunctions, and matched Jaccard between their sets. Layers are matched by relative depth (Pythia L2k against Mamba L4k), Pythia at step 143,000 against trained Mamba. The Pythia slab, its stand-in for what is carried forward, is compared with Mamba's layer state and stack. The comparison is computed after the run, locally, by cross_arch.py from both studies' public files (here: from cross_arch.json).

Observed. Point against point, $a_3$ is 0.31 to 0.99 across matched layers and positions (0.31 to 0.99 at $t = 128$; H7: met, a₃ at t = 128: P6–M12 0.95, P8–M16 0.99, P10–M20 0.99, P12–M24 0.98). Pythia slab against Mamba layer state: 0.00 to 1.00; against the stack: 0.00 to 1.00. Matched Jaccard of the sets: point–point 0.26 to 1.00, slab–state 0.14 to 1.00, slab–stack 0.14 to 1.00 (nulls at most 0.17, 0.17, 0.17). The two T1 root cuts cross-tabulate as 500, 0 / 0, 500 (rows Pythia child 0 / child 1), matched Jaccard 1.00 (null 97.5 % 0.37).

Method

Definitions, the choices I made, what could go wrong and how it was checked, and how to rebuild the page. The construction is the Pythia study's, unchanged; what is new is the recurrent state and its two views, listed under deviations.

Model, probe and cells

Model. state-spaces/mamba-130m-hf at revision 1e76775f628f: Mamba-1, 24 blocks on the residual stream, width 768, inner width 1536, SSM state size 16, conv kernel 4, RMSNorm, residual kept in float32, trained on the Pile (about 300B tokens) with the GPT-NeoX-20B tokenizer. It runs through Hugging Face's reference (torch) implementation of the scan; the fused mamba-ssm and causal-conv1d kernels are not installed. Checkpoints: the pinned trained weights, and MambaForCausalLM(config) after torch.manual_seed(0) (HF's re-implementation of the reference init; no intermediate training checkpoints are published). Transformers n/a, torch n/a.

Probe. The Pythia study's 1,000 snippets, copied verbatim: 200 per source, 128 tokens after an end-of-text token, de-duplicated without labels and shuffled. Both models share the tokenizer backend, so item $i$ is the same token sequence in both studies; the check is described under deviations.

Cells and the state. The model reads each snippet one token at a time with HF's cache, batched over snippets. After each step, a forward hook gives the residual after block $l$ (before the final norm at L24), and the cache gives every layer's conv buffer and SSM state. The conv buffer kept is the last three columns of HF's four-column buffer: the next step discards the oldest column, so only those three are carried forward. Positions 0 to 3 are left out as in the Pythia study.

Views

view$\phi(i)$ at (checkpoint, layer $l$, position $t$)cells
point$h^l_t(i)$, the residual stream after block $l$72
statelayer $l$'s state: Gram average of the conv buffer $c^l_t$ (flattened) and the SSM state $z^l_t$ (flattened), equal weight72
stackthe states of layers $1..l$: Gram average over the $2l$ constituents $\{c^m_t, z^m_t\}_{m \le l}$, all layers (not only the sampled ones); at $l = 24$ the whole state $\Sigma_t$72
bag (reference)$\frac1t \sum_{u \le t} E[x_u(i)]$, the mean input embedding of tokens 1 to $t$one per checkpoint and position

Every vector goes through the same standard step: centre over the $N$ snippets, scale each row to unit length, take cosines, in float64. For the state and stack views each constituent goes through that step on its own, the cosine matrices are averaged with equal weight, and the average is double-centred and renormalised, as the Pythia slab was. This equals the cosine matrix of the concatenated normalised constituents scaled by $1/\sqrt{\#\text{constituents}}$ [thm] (checked in P3). The equal weighting is a choice (D-M1): the conv inputs and the accumulated SSM products have unrelated scales, and raw concatenation would let the parameterisation decide.

Glossary

item, snippet
One of the 1,000 probe texts (a site in the theory's language).
cell
A (checkpoint, layer, position, view); its walk $P_c$ is built from that view.
recurrent state, constituent
Layer $m$'s conv buffer $c^m_t$ and SSM state $z^m_t$ after $t$ tokens; each is one constituent of the state and stack views. The whole state $\Sigma_t$ is all 24 layers' pairs.
block
A run of cells along one axis, with equal weights. Reading block: one layer, positions 4 to 128, trained, one view. Depth block: one position, layers L4 to L24, trained, point view. A single cell is also a block.
walk $P_c$, lazy walk $M_c$
$P_c$ is the Sinkhorn-scaled kernel of a cell (symmetric, rows sum to 1, zero diagonal); $M_c = \frac12(I + P_c)$.
block operator $\bar M$
The mean of the block's $M_c$. Its eigenpairs are $\lambda_k$, $\psi_k$ (with $\psi_0$ constant, $\lambda_0 = 1$).
retention $\rho_c$
$\rho_c(f) = f^\top M_c f / f^\top f$ in cell $c$; $\lambda_k$ is the mean of $\rho_c(\psi_k)$ over the block.
participation number PN
$(\sum_i \psi_i^2)^2 / \sum_i \psi_i^4$: about $N$ for a spread function, small for one sitting on a few items. Below 10 flags a localised mode.
coherent sets
The hard assignment from SEBA's $r$ sparse vectors on $\psi_0..\psi_{r-1}$; unassigned items are zero on all of them.
walk shares $T$, $W$
Equation (2) on the Overview with the grouping by the token at $t$ ($T$) or by source ($W$). Linear in $P$, so a block's value is the mean of its cells' values.
pair mixing ratio $X$
$X_c(A, B) = \frac{N-1}{|A||B|}\sum_{i \in A, j \in B} (P_c)_{ij}$: 1 for a walk that ignores sources.
span agreement $a_r$
Mean $\cos^2$ of the principal angles between the spans of $\psi_1..\psi_r$ of two cells, constant removed; null $r/(N-1)$.
matched Jaccard
Mean Jaccard index of two partitions' sets after the best one-to-one matching (Hungarian); null from 200 permutations, and a ceiling set by the set sizes.
own-source walk share
Per item and point cell, the share of its row of $P_c$ that lands on its own source (validation).
conductance $\phi$, clustering ratio $\Upsilon$
See the zoom.

The zoom, precisely

For a node with snippets $S$ and the block's averaged zero-diagonal walk $\bar P^S$ (rebuilt on $S$), the conductance of $A \subset S$ is $\phi(A) = \sum_{i \in A, j \notin A} \bar P^S_{ij} / \min(|A|, n - |A|)$. Because every cell's walk has the uniform stationary measure, the block's $\phi$ is exactly the mean of the cells' $\phi$ [thm]. Candidates are the level sets of $\psi_1$, $\psi_2$ and $\psi_3$; the cheapest with both sides at least $\max(16, \lceil 0.05 n \rceil)$ wins. With $\mu_k = 1 - \lambda_k(\bar P^S)$, the unconstrained $\psi_1$ sweep satisfies $\mu_1/2 \le h \le \phi_{\text{free}} \le \sqrt{2\mu_1}$ [thm], $h$ being the smallest conductance of any cut; the constrained $\phi^*$ satisfies only $\phi^* \ge h \ge \mu_1/2$. The clustering ratio $\Upsilon = \mu_2/\phi^*$ follows Peng, Sun and Zanetti (2015). For T4 the rebuild on $S$ restricts each constituent's raw inner-product matrix to $S$, double-centres it over $S$, normalises it to a cosine matrix, averages over constituents and then double-centres and renormalises, which is the stack view's own construction applied to the snippets in $S$; restricting the parent's averaged matrix is not the same thing and is not used.

Deviations

From the Pythia study (SPEC sections 1 to 8 of this study, and its README):

  1. The prefix slab is dropped; the state and stack views replace it (D-M4). The training axis is dropped; the HF initialisation is the one comparison checkpoint (D-M3).
  2. C1 splits in two. C1a compares recurrent decoding with the parallel forward pass; HF's Mamba casts parts of the computation to float32 even after .double(), so C1a is a mixed-precision check at 1e-4, not Pythia's float64 gate at 1e-10. C1b, the exact identity, resumes the decode at $t = 64$ from the stored state alone (column 0 of the rebuilt conv buffer is set to NaN, so any read of it would poison the result) and compares with the original decode.
  3. The decode is fed cache_position = max($u$, 3) rather than $u$: HF's decode branch writes the new conv input at that index clamped to 0..3, so the true index below 3 would put it in the wrong column. Every value from 3 on is equivalent.
  4. The probe check is reformulated: the literal check (re-encoding each stored text gives the stored ids) fails on 16 items under Pythia's own tokenizer too, because a snippet can end inside a merge. What is asserted instead: identical tokenizer backends, every id below the vocabulary size, exact decoding of every text, and the same 16 re-encoding failures under both tokenizers.
  5. The cross-architecture comparison goes in its own file, cross_arch.json, made locally after the run.
  6. Layouts: AlignedUMAP for the point grid, and separately for the state and stack grids (the explorer's view switch); the strip is the point view across the two checkpoints.

How to reproduce

The pipeline (explore/mamba_coherent/) runs on Modal: a probe unit, one GPU unit per checkpoint for the recurrent decode, the states and the cosine matrices, one CPU unit per checkpoint for kernels, walks, blocks, statistics, and a final unit for trees, layouts and validation. The cross-architecture comparison and the page are then built on the orchestration machine:

export TMPDIR=/var/tmp/cm-mb
cd explore/mamba_coherent
uv run --with torch --with numpy --with scipy python -I cross_arch.py ../lm_coherent/data/p160t data/_fixture
uv run --with numpy --with matplotlib --with pillow python -I page/build_page.py _fixture
bash page/verify.sh /var/tmp/cm-mb/shots

Construction fingerprint 741175ddc503; data tag _fixture; Modal spend n/a (not yet run). Run ids and the spend table are in explore/mamba_coherent/README.md.
